source.authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

scope: Five remaining Croton species plus five Euphorbia; research-only annotations; prior records unchanged.

records.name: Croton fruticulosus

characters.inflorescence: Terminal racemes; both male and female flowers on one plant
characters.leaves: Croton generic description: simple, alternate to subopposite; precise dimensions absent from 1999 species treatment
characters.fruit: Croton generic three-celled capsule; species measurements not given

records.diagnostic: Woody shrub rather than herbaceous annual Croton species
holds: Leaf margin/size and capsule measurements require secondary regional flora/FNA
1999 cites Bell and Williamson, but BONAP Hays + west/north eligibility not verified
records.flora_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.name: Croton lindheimeri
records.historical_name: Croton capitatus Michx. var. lindheimeri (Engelm. & A. Gray) Müll.Arg. [tentative crosswalk]

characters.habit: Historical Croton capitatus var. lindheimeri: monoecious densely stellate annual, species aggregate 0.2–1(–1.5) m
characters.leaves: Middle-stem to upper-stem petioles become progressively shorter; blades usually acute and sharply tapered from base
characters.habitat: Sandy to calcareous open places, prairies and roadsides (complex)

records.diagnostic: Historical Croton capitatus var. capitatus has near-equal middle/upper petioles, less-pointed blades, uniformly colored seeds
holds: CRITICAL: confirm modern Croton lindheimeri correct basionym and precise taxon concept before accepting identification; not same as Croton glandulosus var. lindheimeri, another taxon separately treated on p.600
Avoid replacing repository's present synonym/taxonomy without nomenclatural audit
records.flora_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.name: Croton lindheimerianus

characters.leaves: Blades thick, often obtuse to acute; genus key says usually suborbicular to oblong-lanceolate
characters.flowers: Three styles bifid to base (six final style branches)
characters.fruits: Three-seeded 3-carpellate capsule; subtending pistillate sepals 4–5 mm

records.diagnostic: Six final style branches, three-seeded fruit, generally shorter pistillate sepals than Croton capitatus; two styles/four tips and one seed in Croton monanthogynus
holds: Confirm contemporary status of both spelling and species distinctness against POWO/FNA
records.flora_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.name: Croton monanthogynus

characters.habit: Closely stellate-hairy monoecious annual up to 50 cm, widely branched
characters.leaves: Rhombic-ovate to elliptic or lanceolate; genus key usually 10–25 mm long
characters.flowers: Two styles yielding four ultimate branches (1999 genus key)
characters.fruits: Fruit circa 4 mm long; characteristically one-seeded mature capsule
characters.habitat: Rocky, eroding or disturbed sites, particularly calcareous soil

records.diagnostic: Two divided styles and mature one-seeded fruit vs three styles/six branches and usually three seeds in Croton lindheimerianus
holds: Document seed reduction without confusing this species with genus Crotonopsis reductions
records.flora_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.name: Croton texensis

characters.leaves: Linear-lanceolate to nearly ovate-oblong, usually 15–35 mm, 3–6 times longer than wide, up to 10–12 mm across; stellate pubescence particularly beneath
characters.flowers: Male and female flowers on different plants; flowers without petals according to genus key; calyces 2–4 mm diameter
characters.fruit: Globose to ovoid capsule 4–6 mm, often weakly warty, stellate-tomentose

records.diagnostic: Dioecy and narrow leaves separate from similarly hairy monoecious Croton; look for verrucose capsule
holds: Texas flora range broad; BONAP county check not completed
records.flora_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.name: Euphorbia angusta

characters.habit: Perennial from woody crown, 6–50 erect stems, each 10–45 cm tall
characters.leaves: Lower elliptical to linear-oblong, 7–25(–38) mm; distal linear leaves more than 9× longer than wide; entire margins
characters.cyathia: Solitary at upper nodes, white gland appendages 2–3× gland width; styles forked only at tip or upper third
characters.fruit: Hairy ovary and capsule according to historical Chamaesyce key; species capsule measurement not given
characters.habitat: Lampasas Cut Plain and south Edwards Plateau margins, at least Burnet and Travis documented historically
characters.phenology: Not visible in retrieved species excerpt

records.diagnostic: Woody-rooted upright perennial with extremely narrow distal leaves and hairy fruits; unlike most prostrate sandmats
holds: Resolve 1999 flora flowering months on continuation and BONAP county-level target range
1999 key upper leaves >9× as long as wide vs current FNA-backed learner >6×; provenance-specific difference retained
records.flora_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.name: Euphorbia bicolor

characters.habit: Erect softly pilose annual to 130 cm
characters.leaves: Middle cauline blades length/width ratio 3–5; upper white-margined bracts typically linear and 5–10× longer than wide
characters.cyathia: Usually 5 involucral glands, petal-like white gland appendages 2–3 mm; latex milky, irritating

records.diagnostic: Hairier and narrower-bracted than Euphorbia marginata; historical flora reports intermediate plants near overlap in Johnson County
holds: Preserve user-approved county-range HOLD; 1999 state-region presence not BONAP county confirmation
Intermediate E. bicolor × marginata morphology flagged: no overconfident photo identification
records.flora_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.name: Euphorbia cyathophora

characters.habit: Nearly hairless annual up to 75 cm
characters.leaves: Mostly alternate; highly variable from ovate/elliptic to narrow-linear, sometimes pandurate/lobed; edges finely toothed to entire
characters.bracts: Upper foliage and flower-associated leaves commonly rosy or rosy-white at the base
characters.cyathia: Usually solitary cup-shaped nectar gland, without appendages
characters.habitat: Stream banks and other open areas

records.diagnostic: Red/pink basal patches and typically alternate stems; gland structure needed to separate uncolored individuals from Euphorbia heterophylla
holds: Poinsettia cyathophora historical segregate not a separate native taxon
Bract coloration variable; no species-only label from that feature
records.flora_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.name: Euphorbia davidii

characters.habit: Usually more robust than Euphorbia dentata; annual taproot herb in current FNA-backed learner
characters.stems: Young growth with comparatively coarse, stiff, slightly recurved hairs
characters.leaves: 1999 key: broadly elliptic, often widest near middle, lower-surface hairs stiff, strongly tapered, with swollen basal cell; predominantly opposite
characters.cyathia: Usually solitary cupped gland without appendages
characters.fruit: Capsule ovoid or broader at base, tapering upward
characters.seeds: Angular-ovoid, coarsely uneven sculpturing, sometimes two transverse dorsal ridges, 2.2–2.7 mm long; caruncle 1.0–1.4 mm wide
characters.habitat: Disturbed ground; original north-central Texas evidence from Eastland County

records.diagnostic: Stiff tapered abaxial hairs and angular/coarsely tuberculate seeds vs E. dentata weak filiform hairs and uniformly fine sculpturing
holds: 1999 reports n=28, versus E. dentata n=14; cytology not usable as normal crew photo trait
Existing taxonomic nativity authority conflict remains unresolved; no BONAP county claim
records.flora_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

records.name: Euphorbia dentata

characters.leaves: Narrow oblong-lanceolate to rhombic-ovate, coarsely shallowly toothed; underside hairs long and weak, not stiff/pustule-based
characters.cyathia: Usually one cup-shaped involucral gland lacking petal appendages
characters.seeds: Rounded to oval, evenly low-tuberculate, 1.7–2.0(–2.2) mm long; caruncle ca. 0.8 mm wide or less
characters.habitat: Stream bottoms, fields, roadsides, disturbed areas

records.diagnostic: Leaf underside long flexible hairs + smaller round evenly sculpted seeds separates from E. davidii
holds: Preserve modern FNA numerical ranges separate from historical 1999 Flora measurements; older key narrower than modern account
records.flora_authority: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
